items.title: Mega-MMDF and DeepfakeBench-MM: Benchmarking Multimodal Deepfake Detection Across Diverse Forgery Pipelines
items.snippet: A large audio-visual deepfake benchmark and standardized evaluation suite show that diverse composite-forgery training improves detection performance but does not reliably generalize to constituent manipulations, while modality masking and temporal misalignment increase detection errors.
items.summary: Mega-MMDF is a large audio-visual deepfake benchmark showing composite-forgery training does not reliably generalize.

items.title: LoopDVR: Looped Transformer for Efficient Dense Visual Recognition
items.snippet: LoopDVR converts pretrained Transformer-based dense visual recognition models into parameter-efficient looped networks by selectively reusing Transformer blocks with adapters, reducing parameters while preserving accuracy.
items.summary: LoopDVR converts pretrained dense visual recognition transformers into parameter-efficient looped networks using adapters.

items.title: Residual Guidance for Real-Time Interactive Video Generation
items.snippet: Residual Guidance is a training-free method that counteracts context inertia in streaming video generation by adding a residual from denoising the previous chunk under the new prompt to early denoising steps, improving prompt switching without training or per-model tuning.
items.summary: Residual Guidance is a training-free method to improve prompt switching in streaming video generation.

items.title: PINE: Point, Instance and Normal Estimation in One-Step Diffusion Model
items.snippet: Understanding a scene requires both geometry and semantics: geometry recovers its spatial structure, and semantics separates it into objects. Current models obtain the two from separate networks or separate passes. We present PINE, a one-step Omni Diffusion Transformer that predicts the point map, the surface normals, and the instance map of an image in one forward pass. PINE treats each map as a token stream, and a stream mask decides which streams interact. A camera-aware ray encoding positio…
items.summary: PINE is a one-step diffusion transformer that predicts point maps, instances and normals together.

items.title: Separating Measurement Failures from Defence Failures in Split Language-Model Privacy
items.snippet: Split-training privacy evaluations fail through distinct mechanisms. Evaluators can overlook an exposed gradient channel, align reconstructions against shifted labels, or deploy uncalibrated probes before testing a candidate defence, while calibrated attacks can also refute real defences. Separating these failure modes alters which claims survive. We conduct a retrospective evidentiary reanalysis across four split-LLM campaigns and two cross-cutting scope checks covering host key custody and va…
items.summary: A paper argues split-training privacy evaluations must separate measurement failures from real defense failures.

items.title: Clinical3D-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Spatial Intelligence of Multimodal LLMs in Hospital Environments
items.snippet: A simulated hospital benchmark shows that multimodal large language models have limited spatial reasoning, while fine-tuning and a 3D-computation method improve their accuracy and reduce the gap to physicians.

items.title: SpatialArena: Where Do Geometric Foundation Models Stand?
items.snippet: SpatialArena is an open benchmark that evaluates geometric models across five 3D perception tasks using uniform metrics and robust alignment, revealing that single-image depth is near saturation on public benchmarks but progress now depends on cross-frame and cross-view consistency.
items.summary: SpatialArena is an open benchmark showing single-image depth is saturated, with progress now needing cross-view consistency.

items.title: Launch HN: Versine (YC F26) – MCP to send and receive money
items.snippet: Hey HN, we’re Harshith, Param, and Vishnu and we're building Versine ( https://versine.com ). Versine lets you send and request money just by talking or texting with your AI (think Venmo with an MCP). We’re software engineers who have worked on distributed systems at Stripe, Databricks, and Amazon. Versine is an MCP that sits in front of a wallet with a balance. With it, your agent can do things like: - Send money to someone with your approval (via passkey in our app) - Send and request money to/from up to 100 people at once - Send money to people without a Versine account (they cash out to their bank in 2 mins) - Pay people without your explicit approval to trusted contacts (you can set this) Here’s a demo: https://youtube.com/shorts/Q9X7zioEqi0 We started working on this because assistants are frustratingly hands-off when it comes to finance and money movement. You can have your assistant go through a receipt and map out all the amounts owed taking care of splitting the subtotal, ta…
items.summary: Versine launched an MCP-based service that lets users send and request money through an AI assistant.

items.title: Distill to Loop: Turning Pretrained Diffusion Transformers into Looped Models with Adjustable Depth
items.snippet: A pretrained diffusion transformer is distilled into a weight-shared looped student that supports variable loop counts at inference and uses depth-wise ODE solvers and loop guidance to match teacher quality with fewer parameters and less compute.
items.summary: A pretrained diffusion transformer is distilled into a weight-shared looped model with adjustable inference depth.

items.title: Show HN: Mason – A lightweight Postgres read-replica, built on columnar storage
items.snippet: Hi HN! TLDR: we’ve built an open-source drop-in replacement for a postgres read-replica, powered by duckdb’s columnar compute engine. It’s very fast. And it looks like postgres. So, this started out as: let’s just connect Clickhouse to our postgres dbs and throw our analytics queries at it instead. That will speed everything up. But we quickly found that 1) Clickhouse comes with quite the learning curve (engine optimisation) to make it fast (we needed something we could easily drop in to any customer’s postgres scenario), and 2) we had underestimated how different clickhouse’s SQL syntax was to postgres. Don’t get me wrong: we love Clickhouse (it’s ridiculously fast if you know what queries to expect), it just didn’t work for our ad-hoc postgres workloads. So we went searching for alternatives that were 1) more plug-and-play and 2) looked a lot more like postgres. We dismissed a bunch based on desk research alone: - pg_mooncake (seems to have stalled since data bricks bought them) - p…
items.summary: Mason is an open-source Postgres read replica that uses DuckDB columnar storage for fast analytics.

items.title: Do learned image captioning metrics generalize? Auditing duplicated samples in human-judgment benchmarks
items.snippet: An audit of recent image captioning evaluation benchmarks shows that duplicate samples and metric behavior inflate reported correlations, and proposes a protocol under which zero-shot vision-language judges perform best on recent test sets.

items.title: Measuring Layer-wise Intrinsic Dimensionality of FFNs in LLMs via PCA
items.snippet: Large language models exhibit a middle-heavy intrinsic-dimensionality profile in their feed-forward layers, and using this profile to guide width allocation improves pruning under a fixed parameter budget.
items.summary: A PCA-based study finds middle-heavy intrinsic dimensionality in LLM feed-forward layers, useful for pruning.

items.title: Foresight Forcing: Learning Spatial Foresight for Robotic Manipulation
items.snippet: Foresight Forcing distills geometry-aware spatial transition queries from a frozen 3D foundation model to improve robotic manipulation action prediction without requiring future observations at deployment.

items.title: Factorized Context Attention: From Emulated to Native Grid Probing
items.snippet: Factorized Context Attention is a training-free block-sparse attention method that natively reproduces grid probing’s span-based attention pattern, encoding input once into a KV cache to match accuracy and extend context at lower cost across video, text, and image tasks.
items.summary: Factorized Context Attention is a training-free block-sparse attention method for extending context at lower cost.

items.title: Align the Pair, Not the Sample: Representation Alignment for Faster and Better One-Step Generato
items.snippet: In one-step generator training, aligning the paired reconstruction path rather than the generative path improves recall and sample quality while accelerating both training stages and lowering FID.

items.title: FATCAT: Fault Injection Attacks Targeting Chip-level Alignment
items.snippet: Model alignment is the primary safety and security mechanism for enforcing refusal of malicious prompts in modern foundation models; yet, existing adversarial evaluations implicitly assume underlying hardware integrity. In this paper, we present FATCAT, the first physical fault-injection attacks capable of eliminating refusal in modern large language and vision-language models. Specifically, we present a non-invasive electromagnetic (EM) fault injection attack targeting GPU-accelerated Systems-…
items.summary: FATCAT demonstrates physical fault-injection attacks that target chip-level model alignment and refusal behavior.

items.title: InstructReplay: Replaying Assistant Turns to Preserve General Behavior During Factual Fine-Tuning
items.snippet: InstructReplay preserves an instruction-tuned language model's general abilities during fact fine-tuning by keeping its responses close to the initial model's answers on general instructions, reducing benchmark decline while still learning new facts.
items.summary: InstructReplay preserves general instruction-following during factual fine-tuning by replaying assistant turns.

items.title: RECAP: Training Long-horizon LLM Agents with Context Compaction
items.snippet: A reinforcement learning framework, RECAP, optimizes context compaction by aligning compressed-context behavior with original-history behavior, improving long-horizon agent performance.
items.summary: RECAP uses reinforcement learning to optimize context compaction for long-horizon LLM agents.

items.title: Small Learned Projections for Semantic-Reversal-Aware Retrieval with Spectral Acceleration: A Four-Domain Empirical Study
items.snippet: Dense-embedding retrievers can fail adversarially: when a query is answered by a document A and reversed by a near-copy B that differs from A by a small meaning-changing edit (a "trap"), raw cosine over E5-Large-v2 places B in the top-10 for 82-100% of queries at a pool of 5,000. We study two things. items.summary: A study finds dense retrievers can be fooled by meaning-reversing near-copies and proposes learned projections to counter this.

items.title: ReFocus: Progress-Guided Adaptive Practice for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation Reinforcement Learning
items.snippet: ReFocus alternates global and local reinforcement learning with DAG-based progress rewards and adaptive practice windows to target task bottlenecks, improving long-horizon manipulation success over a π0.5 baseline.
items.summary: ReFocus alternates global and local RL with progress rewards to improve long-horizon robotic manipulation.

items.title: RoMo Hands: A Large Scale Richly Organized Text to Hand Motion Dataset
items.snippet: A large-scale text-paired dataset of bimanual hand motion, paired with a 393-D representation and benchmark, enables systematic evaluation of generative models for dexterous motion synthesis.
items.summary: RoMo Hands is a large text-to-bimanual hand motion dataset with a benchmark for dexterous motion generation.
